findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: There was observed to not be a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) at the facility at the start of the inspection. CORRECTED- The CFPM arrived during the inspection. Ensure that there is always a CFPM in the facility during all hours of operation and food preparation.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: The handwashing sink at the bar was observed to be out of hand soap. CORRECTED- The PIC replaced the soap in the dispenser. Ensure that all handwashing sinks have a supply of soap at them to allow for proper handwashing.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: SECOND REPEAT- There was observed to be raw steak in a grocery bag in the bottom of a preparation cooler and chopped peppers in a grocery bag in the chest freezer. CORRECTED- These items were moved into other containers and this was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that grocery bags are NEVER used to directly store food in. Grocery bags are not a food-contact surface and cannot be properly washed, rinsed, and sanitized to store food in.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: There was observed to be a gallon of milk that did not have date-marking on it. CORRECTED- The PIC stated that they opened it two days ago and date-marked it during the inspection. Ensure that TCS foods that are opened or prepared in house and kept for over 24 hours are date-marked, with day 1 being the date of opening or preparation and the item being discarded by the end of the 7th day.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment: The bar triple sink’s faucet is observed to be completely off. The PIC stated that it happened a couple of days ago and that they plan to repair it. The facility has the triple sink and dish machine in the kitchen that they can use to clean the bar dishes. Ensure that the faucet is replaced and that plumbing is maintained in good repair.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: A sanitizer bucket was observed to be in the bar handwashing sink. CORRECTED- This was discussed with the PIC and the sanitizer bucket was removed from the sink. Ensure that handwashing sinks are accessible at all times for employee use and are only used for the intended purpose of handwashing.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: There were observed to be cut vegetables stored directly in grocery bags. CORRECTED- This was discussed with the PIC and the vegetables were switched into a ziploc bag. Grocery bags are not a food-contact surface and cannot be sanitized. Ensure that food is stored in a package that protects the integrity of the contents to protect the food from contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The Chlorine sanitizer bucket was observed to test at a concentration of 0ppm of Chlorine. CORRECTED- The sanitizer bucket was remade and tested to be at 100ppm of Chlorine. Ensure that sanitizer buckets are frequently tested and are remade if not at a label-recommended concentration. It is typically recommended to change sanitizer buckets every two to four hours.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The bar gun soda nozzles and the dispenser parts of the soda machine were observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on them. CORRECTED- These nozzles and dispensers were cleaned during the inspection. Ensure that nozzles and soda machines are frequently cleaned to prevent an accumulation of soil residue.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT- There was raw beef observed to be stored directly inside a grocery bag in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- This was discussed with the PIC and the beef was moved into another container. Ensure that plastic grocery bags are never used to store food items directly in, as they are not a food-contact surface.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT- There was a package of raw chorizo in the bottom of the preparation cooler on a shelf above a bag of vegan chorizo crumbles and vegan cheese. CORRECTED- This was discussed with the PIC and the employee. The storage order of the items was switched and the vegan items were moved above the chorizo. Ensure that food is protected from contamination during preparation, holding, storage, and display.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The sanitizer bucket in the kitchen was observed to have a concentration of 0ppm of Chlorine. CORRECTED- The PIC remade the sanitizer bucket and it was discussed to frequently check the concentration of the sanitizer. It is typically recommended to replace the sanitizer every two to four hours, depending on frequency of usage. Ensure that sanitizer is at a label-recommended concentration to make sure that food-contact surfaces are being properly sanitized.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: There was a container of refried black beans that were probed to be at 124F and a container of queso cheese probed to be at 128F in the steam table in the kitchen. CORRECTED- These items were reheated to be above 165F. The black beans were probed to be at 170F and the queso cheese was probed to be at 165F after being reheated. Ensure that TCS food is being hot held at 135F and above.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: There was a container of salsa that is made in-house with a date of 5/20/2026 and a container of mole that is made in-house with a date of 5/8/2026 on it. CORRECTED- These items were past the 7-day date-marking and were voluntarily discarded by the PIC. Ensure that TCS food items are date-marked, with day 1 being the date of opening or preparation and the item being discarded by the end of the 7th day.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: There is not observed to be any Chlorine test strips for the Chlorine sanitizer or Chlorine-sanitizing dish machine in the facility. A follow up is scheduled for 6/11/2026 to ensure that Chlorine test strips have been obtained. Ensure that there are always test strips available in the facility for each type of sanitizer that the facility uses.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: There was not a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) in the facility at the start of the inspection. This was discussed with the PIC. Both operators are CFPMs and they arrived during the inspection. Ensure that there is always a CFPM in the facility during all hours of operation and food preparation.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: There were two containers of raw cut chicken breast observed to be above two whole cuts of beef in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- The chicken was moved to a different shelf, where it was not above the beef. Ensure that staff are educated on storage order to protect food from contamination during preparation, holding, storage, and display.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: There were refried black beans that were probed to be at 121F on the hot holding line. CORRECTED- The PIC stated that the refried black beans were reheated this morning and the black beans were reheated on the stove. The refried black beans were probed to be at 184F on the stove. Ensure that hot food is being held at 135F or above. Ensure that staff are educated to reheat food items to 165F before placing them in hot holding.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: There were multiple food items in the walk-in cooler and in the preparation coolers in the kitchen that were not date-marked, including a container of beans that was made two days ago, a container of pico de gallo that was made yesterday, and a container of cooked meat. CORRECTED- The food items were date-marked and the PIC educated the staff on proper date-marking. Ensure that staff are date-marking TCS food items that are opened or prepared in-house, with day 1 being the date of opening or preparation and the item being discarded by the end of the 7th day, if they are held for more than 24 hours. A spot check is scheduled for 4/13/2026 to ensure that staff are properly date-marking TCS food items.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: There was a container of birria in the walk-in cooler that had a date of 3/21 on it. There were also two containers of salsa that had a date of 3/9 on them. CORRECTED- All of the food items were discarded and the PIC educated the employees that food items made in-house need to be discarded after 7 days. Ensure that TCS food items that are prepared or made in-house are being date-marked and are being discarded by the end of the 7th day. Think day 1 being the date of opening or preparation + 6 days for a total of 7 days.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.comment: There were not signed employee health reporting agreements for any employees. CORRECTED- The facility only has a total of four employees currently and all employees were present at the time. All employees signed an employee reporting agreement. Ensure that these are kept in a safe, accessible place, as these will need to be shown during all health inspections. Employees should be informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with the law, to the person in charge, information about their health as it relates to diseases that are transmissible through food.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment:
The following food was observed to be exposed to contamination due to its packaging:

1. There were observed to be unpackaged tortillas being stored in plastic grocery bags. CORRECTED- The tortillas were voluntarily discarded and the PIC was educated that plastic grocery bags are NOT a food-contact surface. Grocery bags should never be used to directly store unpackaged items into. 
2. There was an opened can of tomato purée in the bottom of the preparation cooler. CORRECTED- The tomato purée was transferred into another container. The PIC was educated that tomatoes are acidic and can erode the can, causing the potential for contamination to the tomato purée. Ensure that cans are never used as a means of storage and that food is always transferred to another container. 

Food packages should always protect the integrity of the contents so that food is not exposed to adulteration or potential contaminants.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: There was a package of raw pigs feet observed to be above empanadas in the bottom of the preparation cooler in the kitchen. CORRECTED- The PIC switched the storage order of the items. Ensure that food is protected from contamination during preparation, holding, storage, and display.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The soda nozzles in the kitchen were observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on them. CORRECTED- The soda nozzles and the dispenser parts of the soda machine were both cleaned during the inspection. Ensure that employees are educated to clean both the soda nozzles and the dispenser parts of the soda machine. Food-contact surfaces should be clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: There was an open bottle of Hidden Valley Italian Dressing and an open bottle of Parmesan cheese that both stated to “Refrigerate after opening” that were observed to be on a shelf at room temperature in the kitchen. CORRECTED- The PIC stated that they had likely been open for days and voluntarily discarded both bottles. Ensure that staff are educated to read labels and are properly storing Time/Temperature Control for Safety (TCS) food items at 41F or below.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: There was a bottle of NyQuil observed to be on a shelf in the kitchen next to a package of tortillas. CORRECTED- The PIC voluntarily discarded the NyQuil and was educated that poisonous or toxic materials should never be above or next to food, equipment, utensils, linens, or single service articles. Ensure that food is not being exposed to contamination from poisonous or toxic materials. The inspector also discussed with the PIC to make sure that employees are not working when sick.
findings.citation_text: 7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: There were not ambient thermometers observed to be in either of the bar coolers. Discussed this with the PIC. Ensure that there are ambient thermometers in all mechanically hot or refrigerated cold holding units.
findings.citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: There were pots and plastic bins observed to be stored on the floor in the kitchen. CORRECTED- The PIC and an employee moved them onto a shelf that is more than six inches above the floor. Ensure that cleaned equipment and utensils are stored at least six inches above the floor.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of repair: 

1. FIRST REPEAT- The cover on the steam table needs removed to allow it to be smooth and easily cleanable. 
2. Seal the hole around the plumbing to the left of the bar handwashing sink. Ensure that the sealant that is used is made to be smooth and easily cleanable. If spray foam is used, ensure that it is cut flush and painted to seal it. 
3. FIRST REPEAT- Paint the bare wood above the triple sink in the bar area. 
4. FIRST REPEAT- Seal the wall board to the trim tiles throughout the kitchen.
5. FIRST REPEAT- Seal the holes in the stainless steel wall behind the cook-line. 
6. FIRST REPEAT- Caulk the drain boards in the dish area. 
7. FIRST REPEAT- Repair or provide stoppers for the triple sink to allow the sinks to hold water. 

Ensure that all repairs are made to be smooth and easily cleanable. Physical facilities should be maintained in good repair.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: There were rat droppings observed to be in the basement in the area with the water heater and ice machine. The PIC stated that these are old droppings. Ensure that these old droppings are cleaned up to allow for monitoring of any rodents. The basement of the facility has a history of a rodent issue and proper cleaning of this area will allow for monitoring of any rodents. A follow up will be conducted on 3/13/2026 to ensure that the droppings have been cleaned.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.
